title: Made in Georgia: How HBCUs Helped Bring ‘A Different World’ From Script to Screen
summary: In the weeks leading up to debut, we brought 'A Different World' to the very communities we celebrate on screen through our “Road to Hillman” tour. We stopped at four HBCUs and predominantly Black institutions.
body_markdown:
School is back in session at Hillman College.


[A Different World](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/a-different-world-sequel-series-new-cast-filming) , the sequel series to the seminal 1987 college-set comedy, debuted Thursday on Netflix — exactly 39 years to the day after the original half-hour premiered. The


[new iteration](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/features/a-different-world-cast-photo-season-1-preview) , which debuted on the


[Global Top 10 English TV list](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/tv) and ranked #2 in the US, follows Deborah, Dwayne Wayne and Whitley Gilbert's free-spirited, well-intentioned, yet rebellious youngest child, as she enters her freshman year at her parents’ famed alma mater.


Welcome to Atlanta


In addition to bringing back


[familiar faces](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/a-different-world-sequel-series-new-cast-filming) on screen (Jasmine Guy, Kadeem Hardison, Darryl M. Bell, Cree Summer, Ajai Sanders, Karen Malina White, Charnele Brown, Dawnn Lewis, Glynn Turman and Jada Pinkett Smith, just to name a few) and off (executive producer and director Debbie Allen, writers-turned-executive producers Gina Prince-Bythewood and Reggie Rock Bythewood), the half-hour comedy hired


290 cast and crew


and


1,800 daily hires and extras


.


Filmed entirely in Atlanta, Georgia over


57 days


,


A Different World


rolled cameras at


11 locations


across the city, including Atlanta Metro State College, Clark Atlanta University, Morehouse College, Spelman College and the Wimbish House. “We couldn't have picked a better place,” said Hardison. “We're doing a show about HBCUs at an actual HBCU.”


HBCU Alumni and Current Students Pitch In Behind the Scenes


But the series didn’t just use local HBCUs as backdrops — it hired alumni and current students in key roles to authentically capture the HBCU experience.


Forty members


of the cast and crew were graduates of HBCUs, ranging from the writer’s room to casting to post-production.


The writer’s room also assembled an HBCU council of current students from across the country who consulted on various issues and events happening on campuses today. When production kicked off in Atlanta, an on-set HBCU council was formed for current students at HBCUs in the Atlanta University Center (AUC). In addition to providing invaluable feedback to the production, these students were able to learn from and shadow different departments on set, from producers and props to costumes and set PAs.


“It means so much to me to be filming at these prestigious HBCUs,” said cast member Kennedi Reece, a recent graduate of Howard University. “Coming from one myself… it's just amazing to be able to experience the different types of culture that each HBCU brings.”


To create more access for local HBCU students and invest in the next generation of entertainment talent, production partnered with Netflix to form the ADW HBCU Student Engagement Initiative. The initiative hired


33 students


as paid, non-union production assistants, shadowing professionals across departments, including accounting, art, costumes, grip, electric, locations, and the writer's room, with scheduling crafted to accommodate their academic schedules.


A Different World


continued to enlist HBCU students and alumni throughout production. In total, roughly


59% of background performers


hailed from HBCUs and about


32%


were current students.


“We've tried to pour as much reality and authenticity into every part of the show as we can,” said co-executive producer/writer Lisa McQuillan. “Behind the camera, it's just been a beautiful Black experience... to work with a crew and a cast and writers in every aspect really feels like a big family reunion or a big HBCU.”


Amplifying Black-Owned Businesses


Behind the scenes,


A Different World


worked with


over 275 vendors and businesses.


The series’ props department also worked with the


[Russell Innovation Center for Entrepreneurs](http://www.russellcenter.org/) (RICE), Atlanta’s home for entrepreneurs, to highlight products from Black-owned businesses across every episode of our season. “It really added to the authenticity,” said creator and showrunner Felicia Pride. “Also, you think about the impact that the show continues to have offscreen.”


[Girl Well](http://www.girlwell.org/) , a non-profit that serves under-sheltered teenage girls by providing self-care kits that promote self-love, also got a shoutout. Founded by Spelman College student Kayli-Joy Cooper, a member of the show’s on-set HBCU Council, Girl Well was featured in Episode 7, where students could be seen constructing kits.


Showrunner and creator Felicia Pride on the set of ‘A Different World.’ (Credit: Quantrell Colbert/Netflix © 2026)


On top of the highly anticipated return of Dwayne Wade’s iconic flip sunglasses, costume designer Provi Fulp (a Clark Atlanta alumna) and her team featured more than


15 Black designers


over the course of the season. This list includes Atlanta-based


[A Ma Maniѐre](https://www.a-ma-maniere.com/) and Caribbean-American fashion designer


[Fe Noel](https://fenoel.com/) . “We're ready to inspire you to go to an HBCU, to dress like Rasheeda, Shaquille, Hazel, Amir and Kojo,” said Fulp, pointing to the new crop of Hillman students.


Enrolling Current and Future HBCU Students Across the Country


In the weeks leading up to the show’s debut, we brought


A Different World


to the very communities we celebrate on screen through our


[“Road to Hillman” tour](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/a-different-world-road-to-hillman-events-schedule) . We stopped at four HBCUs and predominantly Black institutions, including Prairie View A&M in Texas, Chicago State University in Illinois, Hampton University in Virginia and Howard University in Washington D.C. Each stop included photo ops, meet and greets, music and merch giveaways as well as clips and conversations and Q&As with various members of the cast and creative team.


The tour culminated with a return to the AUC to celebrate the premiere on September 21, which kicked off Morehouse College’s 8th Annual Human Rights Film Festival. In addition to talent and VIPs, we opened the doors of Martin Luther King Jr. International Chapel to students, faculty and staff from Spelman College, Morris Brown College, and Clark Atlanta University, allowing us to honor the culture, elevate the legacy and show out for an iconic moment in Black storytelling.


From left to right: Morehouse College president F. DuBois Bowman, ‘A Different World’ cast member Jasmine Guy, Spelman College president Dr. Ayanna Howard and Clark Atlanta University president Dr. George French, Jr. attend ‘A Different World’s’ Special Screening in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images for Netflix)


Netflix Head of Comedy Tracey Pakosta speaks onstage during ‘A Different World’s’ Special Screening in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images for Netflix)


On September 15, we also hosted a special Clips & Conversation event at the Motion Picture Association in Washington, D.C. to share an advanced look at the series. Representative Alma Adams (D-NC), Representative Nikema Williams (D-GA) and Representative Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) offered welcome remarks to celebrate the series and its impact.


From left to right: Netflix US Federal Affairs coordinator Tatum Williams; Rep. Nikema Williams (D-GA); Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA); staff writer Ashley Jackson; cast member Maleah Joi Moon; cast member Darryl M. Bell; creator and showrunner Felicia Pride; Rep. Alma Adams (D-NC); and Netflix Senior Director, US Federal Affairs Diana Oo at the Clips & Conversation event in Washington D.C. (Credit: Kris Tripplaar)


On premiere day, we partnered with Principal for the Day to surprise students at Unity Prep Charter High School in Brooklyn. The cast joined classes, spent time with students, and sat down with juniors and seniors for a college prep conversation. Students shared their aspirations and asked the cast questions about HBCUs and preparing for college— bringing the spirit of Hillman into their own classrooms.


A Different World


is just our latest series to film in Atlanta, joining fan-favorites like


[Stranger Things](https://about.netflix.com/en/news/made-in-america-how-stranger-things-electrified-the-us-economy) ,


[Sweet Magnolias](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/sweet-magnolias) ,


[Beauty in Black](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/beauty-in-black) ,


[Cobra Kai](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/cobra-kai)


and


[Ozark](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/ozark) ,


as well as highly anticipated upcoming shows like


[All the Sinners Bleed](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/all-the-sinners-bleed-series-cast-release-date-news) and


[Scooby Doo: Origins](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/scooby-doo-live-action-series) .


A Different World


is now streaming — only on Netflix.
